titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§260–264: The sons’ rebuke and the western campaigns
part: §§260–264 — The sons’ rebuke and the western campaigns
about: The Sartaul campaign continues. Chinggis rebukes his three sons for keeping Ürüngechi to themselves, is calmed by his quiver-bearers, and sends Sormaqan against the Baqtad; Dorbai-Doqshin is sent against the city of Abtu and Sübegetei against peoples to the north; Jalawachi and Masqud are put in charge of the conquered towns; Bala pursues Jalaldin Sultan and Qan Melig to the land of the Hindus, and Chinggis returns to the Tula. A note on the text: the Mongol is a Ming Chinese-character transcription, and the glosses in square brackets are the Ming glossators’ own; where the English departs from them or is unsure, the note says so.

sentences.t: Žüči, Čaγ̇adai, Ögödei γurban köġüd Örüṅgeči balaγasu oroγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: Jüchi, Cha’adai, Ögödei, three sons, Ürüngechi town having-made-enter,
sentences.i: Jüchi, Cha’adai and Ögödei, the three sons, took in the city of Ürüngechi,
sentences.n: Read this as one long sentence, broken here at its converbs: the three named sons are the subject, and the verb does not come until the third unit. Oroγ̇ulžu is oro- “enter” + the causative -γ̇ul- + the converb -žu (Ming 敎投入着, “making enter”); “took in” (made it come over to them) is my reading, as the glossary also records “making surrender” for this form. Ürüṅgeči is printed Örüṅgeči here and Ürüṅgeči later; the Ming 城名 says only “a town”.

morph.gloss: Jüchi, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Cha'adai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to enter, to go in (verb) [敎投入着]

sentences.t: γurbaγ̇ula balaγad irgen qubijaldužu
sentences.l: three-together, towns people sharing-among-themselves,
sentences.i: and divided the towns and people among themselves, the three together,
sentences.n: γurbaγ̇ula is γurban “three” + the collective -γ̇ula, “the three all together” (Ming 三箇). Qubijaldužu is qubi “share” + -ja- + the reciprocal -ldu- “among themselves” + the converb -žu (Ming 共分着, “sharing out together”); the -ja- is a guess from the Ming. Balaγad irgen “towns, people” are two plain nouns side by side, as the object.

morph.gloss: towns, cities (plural of balaγasun “town”, in -d) (noun, plural) [城子每]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓]
verb-maker from a noun (uncertain; from the Ming)

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a qubi ese γarγažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan-to share not brought-out.
sentences.i: but they gave Chinggis Qahan no share.
sentences.n: Qaγan-a is the dative-locative -a (Ming 行, “to”). Ese “not” (Ming 不曾) negates a past act, and the verb is γarγažuγ̇u: γarγa- “bring out” (γar- “go out” + causative; the stem is read from the Ming 出了) + the narrative past -žuγ̇u. So “did not bring out a share to the Qahan”.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
not (negates a past action; ülü negates present or future) (negative particle) [不曾]
to bring out, put out (γar- 'go out' + causative; stem read from the Ming) (verb) [出了]

sentences.t: Ede γurban köġüd-i baγ̇užu ireġesü
sentences.l: These three sons-(object) descending, when-came,
sentences.i: When these three sons had come and dismounted,
sentences.n: The sons carry the accusative -i (Ming 行, “to”) though they are the ones who come; I take it as marking the subject of this subordinate clause, which is unusual, and cannot be sure. Baγ̇užu is “coming down” (Ming 下着), here “dismounting, making camp”; ireġesü is ire- “come” + the conditional -ġesü, “when (they) came”.

morph.gloss: to come down, dismount, camp (verb) [下着]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Žüči, Čaγ̇adai, Ögödei γurban köġüd-i čimadčü
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan Jüchi, Cha’adai, Ögödei three sons-(object) blaming,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan found fault with the three sons, Jüchi, Cha’adai and Ögödei,
sentences.n: Čimadčü is čimad- + the converb -čü. The Ming glosses it 恠, “blame, find strange”; elsewhere in the glossary the same stem has the sense “find too little”, so I follow the Ming of this passage. The sons stand in the accusative, again glossed 行.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
Jüchi, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Cha'adai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to blame, find fault with (stem as in the glossary; here Ming 恠) (verb) [恠着]

sentences.t: γurban üdür ese aγ̇ulžaγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: three days not caused-to-have-audience.
sentences.i: and for three days did not let them into his presence.
sentences.n: γurban üdür “three days” has no case ending and gives the length of time. Aγ̇ulžaγ̇ulba is aγ̇ulža- “have an audience” (Ming 拜見) + the causative -γ̇ul- + the past -ba, “had them received”; with ese before it, “did not receive them”.

morph.gloss: not (negates a past action; ülü negates present or future) (negative particle) [不曾]
to have an audience, be received (verb) [敎拜見了]

sentences.t: Tende Boγ̇orču, Muqali, Šigi-Quduqu γurban öčirün
sentences.l: There Bo’orchu, Muqali, Shigi-Qutuqu three, when-reporting;
sentences.i: Then Bo’orchu, Muqali and Shigi-Qutuqu, the three, spoke up:
sentences.n: The speech that follows begins at the next unit and runs to bolqu-ju” in U16. Shiratori prints no opening quotation mark; I supply it in `i` only, at U8. Öči- is “report to a superior” (Ming 奏); -rün is the converb of time, “when reporting”. Tende “there” (Ming 那裏) here just means “then”.

morph.gloss: Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Muqali, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Shigi-Qutuqu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to say to a superior, report (verb) [奏]

sentences.t: öčen-melžen aγsad Sartaγ̇ul irgen-ü Soltan-i doroiddaγ̇uižu balaγad irge an-u abuγ̇ai bida.
sentences.l: unsubmitting those-who-were Sartaul people’s Sultan-(object) having-humbled, towns people his took we.
sentences.i: “The Sartaul people were unsubmissive; we humbled their Sultan and took his towns and people.
sentences.n: Öčen-melžen (Ming 不服, “not submitting”) is one word whose inside I cannot parse. Aγsad is a- “be” + the participle with plural -d, “those who were”, so the unsubmitting ones are the Sartaul. Doroiddaγ̇uižu is printed with -γ̇ui-, which is a slip for the causative -γ̇ul- “making bow down” (Ming 敎屈下着): the Han 兀勒 writes γul, not γui. It is the same verb as doroitaγ̇uluγsan-dur in U10; the stem doroida- (the glossary’s lemma for doroidaγ̇ulžu) is itself uncertain. An-u “his” (Ming 他的) comes after its nouns. Abuγ̇ai is ab- “take” + the final past -uγ̇ai; bida is “we” (Ming 咱, the inclusive form).

morph.gloss: unsubmitting, defiant (word uncertain, not parsed; from the Ming 不服) [不服]
past participle with plural -d: those who were
the Sartaul, a people (the Ming 囘囘 'Muslims') (people name) [囘囘]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓 的]
sultan, a title (Ming 王 'king') (noun, title) [王行]
to submit, be subdued (stem uncertain; the glossary's doroida-, apparently a variant of doraita-; printed doroiddaγ̇ui- here) (verb) [敎屈下着]
causative: make … (back-vowel form; the print has -γ̇ui-, a slip for -γ̇ul-: the Han 兀勒 writes γul)
towns, cities (plural of balaγasun “town”, in -d) (noun, plural) [城子每]
people (a form of irgen; the glossary also has irge 'wether') (noun) [百姓]
his, their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
we (inclusive: you and I) (first-person plural pronoun) [咱]

sentences.t: Qubijažu abdaqu Örüṅgeči balaγasun qubijaldužu abqun köġüd bügüde Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-uγ̇ai bi.
sentences.l: Dividing to-be-taken Ürüngechi town sharing-out those-who-take sons all Chinggis Qaγan’s are.
sentences.i: As for the city of Ürüngechi, which was to be taken by dividing: the sons who share it out and take it are all Chinggis Qahan’s own.
sentences.n: The hardest sentence of the speech. Abdaqu is ab- “take” + the passive -da- + the participle -qu, “to be taken” (Ming 被要的); abqun is ab- + -qun, “those who take” (Ming 要的每). The Ming glosses fit my reading, that the sons who divided Ürüngechi and took it are the Qahan’s men, but they give no verb linking the first half, so “which was to be taken by dividing” is uncertain. Qaγ̇an-uγ̇ai is a genitive-possessive (Ming 的; the ending is not certain) with bi “is”.

morph.gloss: verb-maker from a noun (uncertain; from the Ming)
verb-maker from a noun (uncertain; from the Ming)
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
genitive-possessive: belonging to (Ming 的; ending uncertain)
is, exists (verb; perhaps a short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.t: Teṅgeri γažar-a küčü nemegdežü Sartaγ̇ul irgen-i edüi doroitaγ̇uluγsan-dur
sentences.l: Heaven earth-to strength being-added, Sartaul people-(object) this-much when-humbled,
sentences.i: With strength added to us by Heaven and Earth, when we had humbled the Sartaul people thus far,
sentences.n: Nemegdežü is neme- “add” (Ming 添) + the passive -gde- + -žü, “being added”. Teṅgeri γažar-a “Heaven (and) earth” has its dative -a (Ming 行) on the second word only, shared by both. The formula “strength added by Heaven and Earth” returns in U29. Doroitaγ̇uluγsan-dur is the causative “humble” (doroida- + -γ̇ul-) + the participle -γsan + the dative-locative, “at the having-humbled”, that is “when (we) had humbled”. Edüi (Ming 這些) is “so much, thus far”.

morph.gloss: to add (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 添) [被添着]
the Sartaul, a people (the Ming 囘囘 'Muslims') (people name) [囘囘]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓 行]
so much, only this much (adverb) [這些]
to submit, be subdued (stem uncertain; the glossary's doroida-, apparently a variant of doraita-; printed doroitaγ̇ul- here) (verb) [敎屈下了時]

sentences.t: ba olon ere aγta čin-u bajasču maγaižu amui.
sentences.l: we many men geldings your rejoicing maγaižu are.
sentences.i: we, your many men and horses, rejoice, and maγaižu.
sentences.n: Ba “we” (Ming 俺) heads the clause. Olon ere aγta is “many men, geldings”, that is men and horses (Ming 軍 馬). Čin-u “your” (Ming 你的) comes after the nouns, as in-ü and an-u do, and I read it with them, “your many men and horses”, not as “rejoicing in you”; bajasču is “rejoicing” (Ming 歡喜着). Maγaižu has no Ming gloss at all (the bracket is empty in the print) and I cannot parse it; I leave it unread rather than invent a sense.

morph.gloss: we (exclusive; oblique stem man-) (first-person plural pronoun); also 'and' [俺]
your, of you (či 'you', stem čin-, + genitive -u) [你的]
unclear, no Ming gloss (probably a converb in -žu; stem unknown)

sentences.t: Qaγan jakin ein kiliṅlažu amui.
sentences.l: Qaγan why thus being-angry is.
sentences.i: Why, Qahan, are you so angry?
sentences.n: Qaγan has no case ending, so it is either an address (“Qahan, ...”) or a subject (“the Qahan is angry”); the Ming says only 皇帝. Since the three are reporting to him I take it as an address. Jakin (Ming 爲甚) is “why”, ein “thus”, and kiliṅlažu amui is “is being angry”, from a stem kiliṅla- inferred from the Ming 怒.

morph.gloss: to be angry (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 怒) [怒着]

sentences.t: Köġüd buruγ̇u-γ̇an uqažu ajuba-že.
sentences.l: Sons own-fault knowing, feared-indeed.
sentences.i: The sons have understood their own fault and are afraid.
sentences.n: Buruγ̇u-γ̇an is buruγ̇u “fault, wrong” (Ming 不是) + the reflexive -γ̇an, “their own” (Ming 自的行). Uqažu is uqa- “perceive” + -žu. Ajuba-že is aju- “fear” + the past -ba + the particle -že (Ming 也者, “indeed”).

morph.gloss: fault, wrong (noun; Ming 不是) [不是 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form, after a vowel)
to fear, be afraid (verb) [怕了 也者︀]

sentences.t: Qoiči-juγ̇an surtuγai.
sentences.l: Later-for-own let-learn.
sentences.i: Let them learn for the time to come.
sentences.n: Qoiči (Ming 後) is “later, afterwards”; the Ming gloss 自的行 on the ending shows a reflexive, “for their own (future)”, but I do not know how -juγ̇an is built and have entered it as one reflexive ending. Surtuγai is sur- “learn” (Ming 學) + the optative -tuγai, “let them”.

morph.gloss: later, after, the future (noun, adverb; Ming 後) [後 自的行]
reflexive-possessive with dative sense: for one's own (back-vowel form; analysis uncertain)
optative (third person): let it be, let them …

sentences.t: köġüd aburi-jan alγasaγ̇užai.
sentences.l: Sons own-conduct lest-grow-slack.
sentences.i: Lest the sons grow slack in their own conduct.
sentences.n: Alγasaγ̇užai (Ming 懈怠恐, “fear of slackness”) is a stem alγasaγ̇u- “grow slack” (inferred from the Ming) + -žai, which I take as an apprehensive, “lest”, from the Ming 恐. The same ending returns in U26. Aburi “conduct” (Ming 德性) is the printed spelling of the glossary’s abüri.

morph.gloss: conduct, character, temper (noun; printed aburi; the glossary lemma is abüri) [德性 自的行]
to grow slack, become lax (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 懈怠) [懈怠恐]
apprehensive: lest, for fear that (Ming 恐)

sentences.t: Sojurγaγ̇asu aγ̇ulžaγ̇uluγ̇asu bolqu-ju" keġen öčiġešü
sentences.l: Showing-favour if, causing-audience if, will-it-do?" thus-saying, when-reported,
sentences.i: If you show them favour and let them into your presence, would that do?” So they reported.
sentences.n: The closing quotation mark is printed after bolqu-ju”. Bolqu-ju is bol- “be, become” + the participle -qu + -ju, which the Ming 中 麽有 shows to be a question, “will it do?”; the particle -ju is uncertain. Sojurγaγ̇asu and aγ̇ulžaγ̇uluγ̇asu are conditionals in -γ̇asu (Ming 呵, “if”). Keġen “saying” shuts the quotation, and öčiġešü is “when (they) reported” (Ming 奏呵).

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace (verb) [恩賜呵]
to have an audience, be received (verb) [敎拜規呵]
to be, become, do (verb) [中 麽有]
to say to a superior, report (verb) [奏呵]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan žaliražu
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan, anger-calming,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan’s anger subsided,
sentences.n: Žaliražu is žalira- (Ming 怒息, “anger ceased”; stem inferred) + the converb -žu. The whole of Chinggis’s answer is one sentence in Shiratori; I break it into the units U17 to U21 at its converbs.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
to calm down, subside (of anger) (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 怒息) [怒息着]

sentences.t: Žüči, Čaγ̇adai, Ögödei γurban Köġüd-i aγ̇ulžaγ̇ulžu doṅγodurun
sentences.l: Jüchi, Cha’adai, Ögödei three sons-(object) having-caused-audience, while-rebuking,
sentences.i: and he received the three sons, Jüchi, Cha’adai and Ögödei, and, as he rebuked them,
sentences.n: Aγ̇ulžaγ̇ulžu is the causative “had them received” + -žu (Ming 敎拜見着), the same verb as in U6, now without the negative. Doṅγodurun is doṅγod- “rebuke” (Ming 恠說) + -urun, “while rebuking”.

morph.gloss: Jüchi, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Cha'adai, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to have an audience, be received (verb) [敎拜見着]
to rebuke, find fault with (verb; Ming 恠說, 恠責) [恠說]

sentences.t: ötöküs üges örkidčü qaγ̇učin üges qadalžu
sentences.l: elders’ words citing, old words dissecting,
sentences.i: he cited the words of the elders and took the old sayings apart,
sentences.n: Ötöküs is ötögü “old man” + the plural -s (Ming 老的每); üges is üge “word” + -s. Örkidčü (Ming 引證着, “cite as proof”) and qadalžu (Ming 分折着, “split, analyse”) have stems inferred from the Ming alone.

morph.gloss: to cite, adduce (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 引證) [引證着]
to take apart, analyse (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 分折) [分折着]

sentences.t: baiγsan γažar-a baγtaγ̇aldatala maṅlai-jin kölesün arčin jadatala
sentences.l: stood place-to until-entering-peril, brow’s sweat wiping until-unable,
sentences.i: until, on the ground where they stood, they came into danger and could not wipe the sweat from their brows,
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Baiγsan γažar-a is “to the place that stood” (Ming 立了的 地行), perhaps “the ground where they stood”. Baγtaγ̇aldatala (Ming 入險直到, “until entering danger”) I have split as baγtaγ̇alda- + the terminal -tala, leaving the stem unanalysed. Maṅlai-jin kölesün is “the sweat of the brow” (Ming 額 的 汗); arčin (Ming 抹, “wipe”) with jadatala, “until unable”, gives “until they could not wipe it away”.

morph.gloss: to enter into danger (Ming 入險; the stem is not analysed, baγta- “be contained” being only a guess; uncertain) (verb) [入險直到]
terminal converb: until, as far as
to wipe (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 抹) [抹]
to be unable, to fail (verb) [不能直到]
terminal converb: until, as far as

sentences.t: badarkižu čimali-γ̇ar süjü-ġer duγ̇ulγan büküi-dür
sentences.l: expounding, with-reproach, with-teaching, proclamation, while-being,
sentences.i: as he went on expounding, reproaching, teaching and proclaiming,
sentences.n: Four Ming glosses, 說着, 恠責, 敎誨, 宣諭, “speaking, reproach, instruction, proclamation”. Čimali-γ̇ar and süjü-ġer carry instrumental endings, “by reproach, by teaching”; duγ̇ulγan has none. Büküi-dür is bü- “be” + the participle -küi + the dative-locative, “while being”. The nouns čimali, süjü, duγ̇ulγan are my guesses from the Ming.

morph.gloss: to expound, set forth (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 說) [說着]
reproach, blame (noun; word uncertain, from the Ming 恠責) [恠責]
teaching, admonition (noun; word uncertain, from the Ming 敎誨) [敎誨]
proclamation (noun; word uncertain, from the Ming 宣諭) [宣諭]

sentences.t: Qoṅγai qorči, Qoṅtaγar qorči, Sormaqan qorči ede γurban qorčin Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a öčirün
sentences.l: Qongqai quiver-bearer, Qongtaqar quiver-bearer, Sormaqan quiver-bearer, these three quiver-bearers Chinggis Qaγan-to, when-reporting;
sentences.i: Qongqai, Qongtaqar and Sormaqan, these three quiver-bearers, said to Chinggis Qahan:
sentences.n: Qorči and qorčin are both glossed 帶弓箭的, “one who bears the bow and arrows”; I keep “quiver-bearer” as in the earlier parts. The speech begins at boro in U23 with no opening quotation mark printed; I supply it in `i` and the closing mark is printed at ajalasuγai” in U32. The names are Qoṅγai, Qoṅtaγar and Sormaqan, each glossed 人名.

morph.gloss: Qongqai, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
Qongtaqar, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
Sormaqan, a man's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
quiver-bearers, archers (qor 'quiver' + agent -či + plural -n; uncertain) (noun) [帶弓箭的]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
to say to a superior, report (verb) [奏]

sentences.t: boro šibaγ̇un bolija-dur sai oroqu metü
sentences.l: fledgling hawk in-training just entering like,
sentences.i: “Like a young hawk that has only just entered its training,
sentences.n: Boro šibaγ̇un is “fledgling hawk” from the Ming 雛 鷹; boro usually means “grey”, but the Ming gloss decides it here. Bolija-dur (Ming 調習裏, “in the taming”) is a noun I do not otherwise know. Sai is glossed 恰纔 “just now” here, not the usual “good”. Oroqu metü is oro- “enter” + the participle -qu + metü “like”.

morph.gloss: young, fledgling (Ming 雛; elsewhere boro 'grey') (adjective) [雛]
training, taming (noun; word uncertain, from the Ming 調習) [調習裏]
just now (Ming 恰纔; elsewhere sai 'good') (adverb) [恰纔]
to enter, to go in (verb) [入的]

sentences.t: köġüd sai edüi ajalan surun büküi-dür
sentences.l: sons just-now this-much campaigning learning, while-being,
sentences.i: while the sons are only now learning to campaign,
sentences.n: Ajalan (Ming 征進, “go on campaign”) is a stem ajala- inferred from the Ming + -n; surun is sur- “learn” + -un. The two converbs sit before büküi-dür “while being”, so “while learning to campaign”. Edüi again “only this much”.

morph.gloss: just now (Ming 恰纔; elsewhere sai 'good') (adverb) [恰纔]
so much, only this much (adverb) [這些]
to go on campaign (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 征進) [征進]

sentences.t: köġüd-i šiṅtalun mene metü jakin ein doṅγodumu.
sentences.l: sons-(object) back repeatedly like, why thus rebuking?
sentences.i: why rebuke them so, as if they were shrinking back time after time?
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Šiṅtalun (Ming 退後, “retreat, behind”) and mene (Ming 頻煩, “repeatedly, troublesomely”) are words I cannot parse; with metü “like” I read “as if (they) kept drawing back”. The sons carry the accusative again (Ming 行). Doṅγodumu is doṅγodu- “rebuke” (Ming 恠責有), the glossary’s doṅγodu- (a variant of doṅγod- in U18), + the present -mu.

sentences.i: If you send us, the Töbödüd, inciting your own dogs,
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Man-i is ba “we” (exclusive, Ming 俺) in its oblique stem man- + the accusative. Töbödüd the Ming glosses 西番每, “Tibetans”; I cannot fit it into the sentence (an apposition, “us, the Töbödüd”, is the least strained) and have left it as printed, in `i` too, as a people-name. Nogod(i)-jan is noγai “dog” + plural -d + the reflexive, “one’s own dogs” (Ming 狗每 自的行); tukirču is tukir- “incite” (Ming 唆) + -ču; ileġesü is ile- “send” + the conditional. The English “inciting your own dogs” keeps the words as they stand; a comparison (“as one sets one’s dogs on”) is a guess the text does not write.

sentences.i: and it was said that they knew them in accord with what is right;
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Josun-dur adali is “like (in accord with) the right” (Ming 理行 相似), and kelelegdežü is kele- “speak” + the passive -gde- + -žü, “being spoken (of)” (Ming 被說着). The Ming glosses meden 知, “know”, here, whereas in the next units mede- is 管, “manage”. Who says it is not stated.

sentences.t: köġüd-i in-ü Masqud, Qurumši-ji bidan-u daruγas- luγ̇a
sentences.l: son his Masqud, Qurumshi-(object) our governors-with
sentences.i: his son Masqud the Qurumshi, together with our governors,
sentences.n: Köġüd-i is plural in form for a single son, as in U50 (Ming 兒子(每)行). In-ü “his” (Ming 他(的)) is set before the name. Qurumši-ji is the clan name with the accusative. Daruγas-luγ̇a is printed in two pieces, daruγas- and luγ̇a, and counted as two words: daruγa + plural -s + the comitative -luγ̇a (Ming 鎭守的(每) 一同), “together with the governors”. Bidan-u “our” (Ming 咱的) is the inclusive form.

sentences.t: Buqar, Semisgen, Ürüṅgeči, Udan, Kisqar, Urijaṅ, Küsen-Daril teriġüten balaγad-i medeġülün tüšižü
sentences.l: Buqar, Semisgen, Ürüngechi, Udan, Kisqar, Urijang, Küsen-Daril and-the-rest towns-(object) making-manage entrusting,
sentences.i: he put in charge of the cities of Buqar, Semisgen, Ürüngechi, Udan, Kisqar, Urijang, Küsen-Daril and the rest,
sentences.n: Seven names, each glossed 城名, “a town”. Teriġüten is teriġü “head” + -ten, with the Ming 等 “and so on”; as in earlier parts I read it “and the rest”. Medeġülün is mede- + the causative -ġül- + -n (Ming 敎管, “make manage”); tüšižü is tüši- “entrust” (Ming 委付着).

sentences.t: ečige-ji in-ü Jalawači-ji abčiražü Kitad-un Žuṅdu balaγasu medeġülün abčiraba.
sentences.l: father-(object) his Jalawachi-(object) taking-along, Kitad’s Zhongdu town making-manage, brought.
sentences.i: and he took along his father Jalawachi and brought him to take charge of the Kitad capital, Zhongdu.
sentences.n: Žuṅdu is Shiratori’s reading; the Ming glosses the city 大都 (“great capital”), and I give the form as Zhongdu, as before. Kitad-un is “of the Kitad” (Ming 契丹), the realm of northern China. Abčiražü … abčiraba is “taking along … brought”, a pair of verbs on one stem. Abčiražü is printed with -žü after a back-vowel stem, as jadažü is elsewhere.

sentences.t: Sartaγtai küġün-(n)eče Jalawači, Masqud qojar-un balaγasun-u töre josun čidaqu-jin tula
sentences.l: Sartaγtai men-from Jalawachi, Masqud two’s town’s rule principle able-ones’ because,
sentences.i: Because these two, Jalawachi and Masqud, out of the Sartaul men, were able in the rules and principles of a city,
sentences.n: Sartaγtai is glossed 囘囘, “Muslims”, as Sartaγ̇ul is, and is Sartaγ + -tai (I take it for the Sartaul); küġün-(n)eče is küġün “man” + the ablative, with the (n) Shiratori’s (Ming 人處). Čidaqu-jin is čida- “be able” + -qu + a genitive-like -jin (Ming 能的(的)); it is hard to say how it hangs, and the word order töre josun is the reverse of josu töre in U51. Tula (Ming 上頭) is “because of”.

sentences.t: Kitad irgen-i medeġülün daruγas-luγ̇a tüšibe.
sentences.l: Kitad people-(object) making-manage governors-with entrusted.
sentences.i: he entrusted the Kitad people to their management, together with the governors.
sentences.n: The finite verb of the clause that gives the reason in U55: tüšibe is tüši- “entrust” + the past -be. The Kitad (Ming 契丹) here are the people of the northern realm, as in U55.

sentences.t: Sartaγ̇ul irgen-dür doloγ̇an hod jabužu
sentences.l: Sartaul people-among seven years going,
sentences.i: After going about among the Sartaul people for seven years,
sentences.n: The subject is not stated until U65; it is Chinggis. Hod is hon “year” + the plural -d (Ming 年(每)); jabužu is jabu- “go” + -žu. The dative-locative -dür, Ming 行, gives “among”.

sentences.t: Žalaldiṅ Soltan, Qān Melig qojar-i Hindus-un γažar-a kürtele nekežü
sentences.l: Jalaldin Sultan, Qan Melig two-(object) Hindus’ land-to up-to pursuing,

sentences.t: Hindus-un kižiγ̇ar irgen-i daγ̇uliγ̇ad olon temeġed olon serkes-i abuγ̇ad irežüġüi.
sentences.l: Hindus’ border people-(object) having-plundered, many camels, many wethers-(object) having-taken, came.
sentences.i: and, plundering the people on the border of the Hindus and taking many camels and many wethers, came back.
sentences.n: Serkes is glossed 羯股; 羯 is “wether, castrated ram” and the sense of 股 is unclear, so “wethers” is tentative. Daγ̇uliγ̇ad and abuγ̇ad are converbs in -γ̇ad, “having plundered, having taken”; irežüġüi is ire- “come” + the narrative past.

sentences.t: Tende Čiṅgis Qaγan qarižu žaγ̇ura Erdis-i žusažu
sentences.l: There Chinggis Qaγan turning-back, midway Erdis-(object) summering,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan turned back from there and spent the summer on the way, at the Erdis,
sentences.n: Tende “there” (Ming 那裏) here means “from there”. Žaγ̇ura is “midway, on the way” (Ming 路間). Erdis is glossed 地名行, “a place”, with an accusative, so “spent the summer at the Erdis”. Žusažu is žun “summer” + the verb-maker -sa- + -žu.

sentences.t: dolodiγ̇ar hon takija žil namur Tula-jin Qara Tün-(n)e ordos-tur baγ̇uba.
sentences.l: seventh year, Hen year, autumn, Tula’s Black Forest-in, palaces-in, came-down.
sentences.i: In the seventh year, the Hen year, in autumn, he camped in his palace tents in the Black Forest of the Tula.
sentences.n: Dolodiγ̇ar is doloγ̇an “seven” + the ordinal -diγ̇ar (Ming 第七), the same seven as in U58; takija žil is “the Hen year”, in the twelve-year cycle. Tula-jin is “of the Tula” (Ming 河名 的), and qara tün “black forest” (Ming 黑 林). Ordos-tur is ordo + plural -s + the dative-locative (Ming 宮(每) 裏). Baγ̇uba is “came down”, here “camped”. The passage ends.
